item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial judge denies mistrial request, reprimands prosecution
item.description: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony ended abruptly Monday in Plymouth Superior Court when a witness began speaking about religion and the defense unsuccessfully called for a mistrial.

item.title: Women left behind in high-paying AI job boom, LinkedIn research finds
item.description: While hiring for AI companies is booming, women are getting left behind, according to new research from LinkedIn. It found that female candidates accounted for 26% of hires for jobs requiring AI skills in the U.S., compared to 50% of women hired into non-AI positions. Sarah Steinberg, the head of global public policy partnerships at LinkedIn, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Body of wife wanted in Worcester, Massachusetts, police officer's death found
item.description: Karen Solomon​, wanted for questioning in the death of her Worcester, Massachusetts, police officer​ husband, has been found dead after a massive search.

item.title: Breaking down Scott Bessent's comments on Canada, tariffs, Mark Carney
item.description: The U.S. is imposing a 50% tariff on $20 billion in Canadian goods. Canada vowed to retaliate with tariffs of their own that would go into effect on Sept. 8. Rob Russo, a Canadian correspondent for The Economist, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Supreme Court allows Trump to implement parts of order restricting mail voting
item.description: The Supreme Court divided 6-3 in granting the Trump administration's request for emergency relief.

item.title: Massachusetts woman suspected of killing husband found dead
item.description: Karen Solomon, a Massachusetts woman wanted for questioning in the death of her police officer husband, has been found dead, Worcester authorities announced on Monday. Law enforcement called the case a "tragic murder-suicide."

item.title: 8-year-old girl dies from brain-eating amoeba infection in Louisiana
item.description: Lillian Smart, 8, has died after being infected by an extremely rare brain-eating amoeba that is found in warm freshwater, her family said.

item.title: Why Trump's Canada tariffs are likely to have a modest impact on prices
item.description: Although some Canadian goods will get more expensive in the U.S., trade experts don't expect a broader inflation spike.

item.title: Sean Grayson, convicted in killing of Sonya Massey, dies in prison, attorney says
item.description: Grayson, 32, was found guilty last October of second-degree murder for the shooting of Sonya Massey and was serving a 20-year sentence.

item.title: Judge in Lindsay Clancy case rejects defense's call for mistrial
item.description: The judge presiding over the Lindsay Clancy murder case rejected the defense's push for a mistrial on Monday. Clancy has admitted to killing her children but has pleaded not guilty, arguing that postpartum psychosis caused her actions. CBS News correspondent Shanelle Kaul and legal contributor Jessica Levinson have the latest.

item.title: U.S. unveils new Iran sanctions after Trump threatened "economic D-Day"
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said new sanctions being imposed on Iran would amount to the "greatest financial offensive" ever.

item.title: Gen Xers fret over Social Security. "I will likely be working in retirement."
item.description: Millions of Generation X Americans expect to depend on Social Security as their main — or only — source of retirement income.

item.title: Stars and Stripes reporter says independence "has to be instituted in practice"
item.description: Lara Korte, a Stars and Stripes reporter who was dismissed last week, told CBS News on Monday that the paper's editorial independence remains paramount.

item.title: What does an employer need to post a job online?
item.description: Posting a job online can be simple, but employers still need to get the important details right before going live.

item.title: Bessent announces campaign to create "economic onslaught" against Iran and its partners
item.description: The Trump administration is trying to pull all economic levers at its disposal to cripple Tehran.

item.title: How much will a $50,000 home equity loan cost monthly if opened this September?
item.description: A $50,000 home equity loan

item.title: Trump announces 50% tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports
item.description: President Trump said tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports will rise to 50% on Jan. 1, 2027, in a social media post.

item.title: Iran-linked hackers took U.K. power plant offline for first time, reports say
item.description: The attack happened the same month Iranian-linked hackers are believed to have targeted the water systems of a dozen U.S. states.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 23)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Prosecution in Lindsay Clancy trial focuses on psychological experts in rebuttal testimony
item.description: The prosecution in the Lindsay Clancy trial continues to call rebuttal witnesses, mainly focusing on the psychological aspects of Clancy's state of mind when she killed her 3 children. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul and legal contributor Jessica Levinson have more.

item.title: Redfin and Zillow must change agreement that hurts competition, FTC says
item.description: Federal regulators alleged that a $100 million deal between Redfin and Zillow stifled competition for apartment listings.

item.title: Out-of-control Hawk Fire in Reno keeping tens of thousands evacuated
item.description: Shifting winds challenged firefighters battling the out-of-control Hawk Fire in Reno, Nevada, that was keeping tens of thousands of people evacuated.

item.title: Washington Post ordered to reinstate columnist fired after Charlie Kirk posts
item.description: The ruling said the newspaper did not have sufficient cause to terminate Karen Attiah, who at the time was the last Black full-time member of the Post's opinion desk.

item.title: The best new restaurants of 2026, according to Bon Appétit
item.description: Bon Appétit has released its 2026 list of the best new restaurants in the U.S. Editor-in-Chief Jamila Robinson joins CBS News alongside Kabawa chef Paul Carmichael to discuss the fresh additions.

item.title: Ex-NBA center ejected from WNBA game after being confronted by player
item.description: The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women should be allowed to participate in the league.

item.title: Tourist dies in Death Valley after car gets stuck in 116-degree heat
item.description: A 68-year-old French tourist died in Death Valley National Park last week after becoming trapped in 116-degree temperatures.

item.title: 4 arrested after world champion boxer shot dead in South Africa
item.description: Zolani Tete made history in 2017 when he took just 11 seconds to knock out his opponent with his first punch to retain his WBO bantamweight crown.

item.title: Trump puts autistic kids in the spotlight and cuts agencies built to protect them
item.description: Researchers and disability rights advocates warn that the dismantling of the Education Department and its erosions of civil rights oversight risk widening the disparities autistic children face.

item.title: Videos show Hawk Fire spreading around Reno, Nevada, prompting thousands to evacuate
item.description: As the Hawk Fire encroached on Reno, Nevada, on Sunday, around 90,000 people were forced to evacuate. Officials said they believe the flames are "human-caused," and Gov. Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency in part of the state. Videos show the blaze and the firefighting efforts. Some videos do not include sound.

item.title: Robin Wall Kimmerer on the wonders of nature
item.description: The botanist's bestselling books, "Braiding Sweetgrass" and "The Serviceberry," advocate for living and working in collaboration with the Earth, and sharing the gifts of nature - ideas, she says, some may see as subversive.
